main_text.p: uerò non. Vnde dicit Augustinus: Fides est, credere quod non uides. Hæcille.

Etsi abstinedum nobis est à λογομαχίας[?], & fatendum uocabula quædam aliter in Philosophia, quàm in Theologia, usurpa-ri:tamen in hac definitione illud probari non debet, quòd sic definit fidem, ac si es-set τῶν ἐφ' ἡμῖν[?], seu ut magis theologicè loquar, ac si à natura eiusq; uiribus, tanquàm suis principijs, non autem à gratia diuina, ortum ea duceret. Constat autem, fidem esse eximium & gratuitum Dei donum. Sed ad singula eius membra quædam διὰ βραχέων[?] annotabimus.

•. Si fides certitudo est, cur Pontificij fideles iubent ambigere, an'ne in gratia sint? cur nobis temerariæ præsumtionis notam aspergere conantur, cum audiunt affirmantes, Certò persuasos nos esse de bere de Dei erga nos beneuolentia? Pugnant extremè fides quæ certitudine definitur, & dubitatio. Quomodo ergo pœnantia in gradibus excellentibus, possunt esse in eodem subiecto, uidelicet in corde hominis?
2. Si etiam uoluntariam ideo uocant, quòd ab intelligentia & uoluntate humana

page.notes: Printed mark "•." before the second paragraph is read as a bullet-like sign; marker "2." before the last paragraph is uncertain. Greek words are read from a small scan and marked [?]; the accents and the exact form of the second and third Greek words are doubtful. The first letter of "gratia" line and "pœnantia" (read as pœnitentia? printed "pgnantia") is doubtful: printed as "pgnantia" with a fused initial, transcribed as "pœnantia" [?]. The line "ri:tamen" has a colon that may be a scan artifact. "fi-deles" hyphens are printed line-end hyphens.
